questions.prompt: What is the main job of a command interpreter?
options: Fetch a command from the user and execute it

questions.prompt: On a system that offers several command interpreters to choose from, what is each one called? (one word)
A command interpreter is always part of the kernel.
In UNIX, most commands are implemented as:
options: Separate program files that the shell finds by name and runs
Code built into the shell itself

questions.prompt: A programmer writes a new command-line tool. With the program-name approach, what must change in the shell?
options: Nothing; the new program file just needs to be where the shell looks
The user must switch to a different shell
The shell must be recompiled with the new code

questions.prompt: Why does `cd` have to be a built-in command?
options: Programs aren't allowed to read directories
It changes the shell's own current directory, which a separate program can't do for it
It needs to run in kernel mode
It's too short to be a program

questions.prompt: bash and zsh are both shells: different command interpreters that do the same basic job.
